portInfo.description: Canaveral Port Authority publishes a cruise-terminal map and arrival guides listing seven passenger terminals in Cape Canaveral, FL 32920. North-side A terminals sit on Charles Rowland Drive; south-side B terminals use Discovery Road / Christopher Columbus Drive. Directions & Parking states parking is adjacent to each terminal (no shuttle), that the port does not take parking reservations, that ship schedules and assigned terminals are subject to change, and that parking opens at 10 a.m. for embarkation. From Orlando International Airport (MCO) the port describes about 45 minutes west-to-east via S.R. 528 East to Exit 54A or 54B. Door pins remain null.

climate.description: Humid subtropical climate with hot summers and mild winters

politics.visaRequirements: Visa-free for citizens of Visa Waiver Program countries (ESTA required). Others need visa.
politics.entryRequirements: Valid passport required. ESTA required for visa-free countries. Some nationalities need visa.

thingsToDo.intro: Pick one neighbourhood or excursion scale and keep time for the gangway queue on the way back.
topThings: Cocoa Beach / Jetty Park area — shorter transfer than Orlando theme parks — ~120 min.
Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex — half-day minimum — ~240 min.
Cape Canaveral lighthouse area — timing Not verified.
Orlando theme parks — embarkation-eve hotel nights only; not a realistic same-day turnaround.
thingsToDo.shortCall: Stay near the port area and keep a generous buffer before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.standardCall: Combine a central walk, one attraction, and lunch if times allow—start back well before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.longerCall: A second stop or coach outing is realistic only with confirmed transport and an eight-hour or longer window.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: Know your Exit 54A vs 54B before the toll road fork — north and south terminal clusters are different exits.
